explanation: Two triggers: (1) a text-opening conjunction or interjection ('And', 'Then', 'But', 'Oh', 'Love' as the first word of the text, or right after leading newlines) fires on that token whatever follows, including business text; (2) evocative nature, time-of-day, weather, body/sense, emotion, colour or taste words and a simile 'like' after such description (night, wind, cloud, voice, eyes, blood, love, sweet, blue, 'glowing like') fire when they fall within the first few words of a text or follow emotional, lyrical or narrative description, but are mostly suppressed after a full business or technical clause ('The finance team said the voice...'); 'night' is the exception and often still fires there. Text made only of business, administrative or technical vocabulary that does not open with one of those words stays inactive (20 of 20 varied measured sentences peaked at <= 0.01 of max).
